name: Bold
label: Revelation
lede: Four Westchester kids who were too young to get into CBGB made one album in Youth of Today's studio, lifted the cover idea from Run-D.M.C., and watched it outlive the band by decades.

eras.title: Too young for the door
eras.text: Katonah is forty miles north of the city, and Matt Warnke was 13 or 14 when he found hardcore through record shops, fanzines and friends' older siblings. He and his John Jay High School friends were playing CBGB matinees before most of them could legally walk in.

years.p: Warnke on vocals and guitar, Tim Brooks on bass, [[Drew Thomas|ebc66701-0d59-49c9-ae21-4937edb96a6a]] on drums. Warnke's first trips to CBGB mean standing outside; he's under 16. The record that hits hardest is [[Agnostic Front|40b8a690-94e4-4c82-ad0f-73f4b841e46a]]'s Victim in Pain.
Crippled Youth record the songs that become their debut 7". It's the earliest material Revelation would later gather on The Search.
Out on Mike Trouchon's California label, with a feature in Maximum Rock'N'Roll. The first sleeves went out with the layout ruler accidentally left in under the back-cover photo.

years.h: First CBGB matinee: with [[Warzone|496da466-68e9-4cbb-9e86-cbb57eda861a]] and [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]]
years.p: Warnke's first official show at the Bowery club, on a bill with [[Rest In Pieces|3cb8bd68-6c42-4dea-b0c6-f33c66cc790b]], Warzone and Youth of Today. John Zuluaga, known to everyone as Zulu, comes in on guitar and Warnke moves to vocals only.
years.xp:
Warnke had been going to CBGB since 1985, but under 16 that mostly meant hanging around outside. The June 1986 matinee was his first time through the door officially, and he was on stage.

The same van rides into the city delivered the other big shock of that year: hearing the [[Cro-Mags|9ffa627f-32c2-4cb1-bfad-00cf348abc70]] demo, which Warnke remembers as a cultural shift.

eras.title: Speak Out
eras.text: By the time the kids had a full-length in them they'd dropped the name Crippled Youth for Bold, and a California label was lined up to put the album out. Then Jordan Cooper made his case, and it became Revelation No. 9.

years.h: Wishing Well loses the record to Rev
years.p: Speak Out was meant for Pat Dubar and Pat Longrie's Wishing Well in Orange County. Jordan Cooper talks the band into bringing it to Revelation instead.

q: At the time, I was definitely not thinking about longevity.
years.p: Recorded at Electric Reels with Dan Nichols producing, the studio where Youth of Today had cut Break Down the Walls. The working title was Reach Out.
years.xp:
The look came from outside hardcore. Warnke pointed to Run-D.M.C.'s Raising Hell and Stetsasonic's On Fire for the tinted photos and block logo, and Van Halen's first album for the quadrant layout.

About ten years later the record got a second life, as a straight edge revival in Ohio spread outward and new kids went looking for the originals. Zulu admits nobody in the band was thinking that far ahead.

eras.title: Three songs and a second album nobody heard yet
eras.text: With Tom Capone adding a second guitar, Bold got heavier and more careful. They cut one more 7" and a second record in 1989, then scattered into the bands that pushed New York hardcore somewhere new.

years.p: Three songs. The colored vinyl was supposed to be maroon to match the sleeve, but the plant couldn't mix it right and it came out pink.
Bold's final recordings are done by February 1989: the songs that become Looking Back.
Thomas helps start [[Into Another|c235e5fd-4144-4e53-95ff-b33dc5f239c8]] in 1990. Capone goes on to [[Quicksand|3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32]], and later Handsome and Instruction.
The 1989 session sees release two years after it was cut. Rev later reissues it as a 12" with two bonus tracks.

eras.title: The Bold that wasn't
eras.text: Warnke got back on stage with a new band that played some old Bold songs and had no name of its own. A Connecticut flyer solved that problem for them, and not everyone was happy about it.

q: This isn't BOLD, but we're going to do some of those songs.
years.h: Billed as Bold at the New Milford Teen Center
years.p: Warnke with Eddie McNamara, Chris Daley and Matt Martin had already played the Wetlands and CBGB. Booked in Connecticut, they were billed as Bold, and people took it for a reunion.
years.xp:
The band had no settled name and was mixing Bold songs into a new, post-hardcore set. McNamara's line to the crowd was blunt about it.

The real reunion, with the Speak Out core, was still nine years away.

eras.title: The real reunion
eras.text: Revelation's retrospective brought Bold back together, with an old friend from Youth of Today and Judge on second guitar. By the label's 25th birthday they were a fixture of its anniversary bills on both coasts.

years.p: Sixty-six minutes: Looking Back, Speak Out, compilation tracks, two unreleased songs and the Crippled Youth 7", running backwards in time from the last session to the first.
Warnke, Capone and Brooks, with Vinny Panza on drums and [[John Porcelly|dff848b4-bb79-445a-81e1-3db65b7ddd3e]] sitting in on second guitar.
The singer and the guest guitarist leave the reunion line-up.
Bold on the West Coast leg of the label's 25th anniversary.
The New York leg, back in the city whose matinees they grew up in.

eras.title: Thirty-five and embossed
eras.text: Revelation gave Speak Out the full anniversary treatment, and the band kept playing to people who weren't born when it came out.

years.p: A remaster in an embossed gatefold with a 40-page booklet designed by John Scharbach, plus color variants and a cassette.

years.h: On the road with Youth of Today
years.p: An East Coast run with Youth of Today, after West Coast dates earlier in the year.
